title: OpenRTB 3.0 AdCOM audio placement answered via bid.media.ad.audio.adm

source.name: IAB OpenRTB 3.0 transaction examples plus AdCOM 1.0 Placement.audio / Ad.audio objects
source.notes: All source records are retained in assets/sources.json by reference.sourceIds.

modifications: All auction, bid, creative, app and publisher identifiers are synthetic.
All domains use reserved .test names; no real user IDs, IP addresses, consent strings or tracker endpoints.
device.ip is the documentation-only address 192.0.2.14; OS values describe a synthetic test device.

Currency is kept USD end to end (request cur[], item.flrcur, response cur, bid price) to isolate the audio-specific plumbing from the unrelated 3.0 currency-envelope defect already recorded as DEF-105 on bn-banner-30-adcom.
provenance.sanitized: Only synthetic identifiers, original fixture creative, reserved domains and TEST-NET addresses. No live tokens, subscriber IDs or real tracking URLs.

pairApplicability.note: Every response bid references an offered impression/item; auction identifiers match.

specNotes: AdCOM Placement.audio requires only mime[]; there is no duration/ctype-equivalent requirement on the 3.0 audio request path (contrast video, which also gets ctype/mindur/maxdur checks).
AdCOM Ad.audio carries adm or curl exactly like display/video; this fixture supplies adm.

format-detect.js's 3.0 response sniff only runs isVastShape() against ad.video.adm, never ad.audio.adm — so, unlike the 2.x response path (DEF-101), a VAST-shaped 3.0 audio creative is NOT mis-tagged FORMATS.VIDEO here. format.formats is expected to stay audio-only.

rules-response-30.js never calls validateVast() on ad.audio.adm even when it is VAST-shaped (it does for ad.video.adm) — an asymmetry between the video and audio branches of the same function. This fixture's adm is deliberately spec-valid VAST, so the asymmetry produces no visible difference here (zero vast.* findings either way); it is not asserted as a failing expectation because a valid document cannot distinguish 'not validated' from 'validated and found clean'. Demonstrating the asymmetry concretely needs a deliberately broken 3.0 audio adm, which is mutation-category territory, not a base pair.

crosscheck.js's projectItem30/projectBid30 never copy placement.audio or read ad.audio.adm, so this audio bid is invisible to every adm-dependent crosscheck rule (video-VAST, native, pop-landing) — none of those apply to an audio-only item anyway, so the generic id/impid/floor crosscheck checks below are unaffected and pass.

Currency is kept USD end to end here specifically to avoid the already-recorded 3.0 currency-envelope defect (DEF-105); that defect is general to 3.0, not audio-specific, and is out of scope for this fixture.
notes: Core observations in the source archive were deliberately excluded from expectations. Protocol metadata may describe a vendor-specific 2.x carrier; it does not claim a normative minor-version inference.

preview.capabilityGap: The current VAST preview is inert XML; audio playback is not implemented. This applies identically whether the creative arrived via a 2.x bid.adm or a 3.0 bid.media.ad.audio.adm.
